items.title: Workflow SDK adds idempotent starts
items.summary: The 's  function can now admit a run and claim a hook in one atomic step. Duplicate workflow starts fail safely. The atomic start replaces the previous -then- pattern, whose gap between the lookup and the start left a documented duplicate-start race.Workflow SDKstart()getHookByToken()start()The claimed Hook exists from the moment the run is admitted, so  works even before the run begins executing, and early payloads are buffered and delivered in order. Inside the workflow,  with the same token binds to the already-claimed hook: guaranteed, registering nothing new, adding no step, and resolving  to .resumeHookcreateHook({ token })getConflict()nullThe token is the idempotency key, and it comes from your own domain: an order ID, an invoice ID, an import ID, or a request ID. The token alone guarantees idempotency. Exactly one run owns it, and a duplicate  throws  carrying the owner's  and never becomes a run. The workflow doesn't have to open the hook at all, and if it never does, the token was only an idempotency key and the run completes normally.start()HookConflictErrorconflictingRunIdSetting  keeps the token unavailable after the run ends, counted from , so late duplicates are still refused.experimental_minRetentionstart()Upgrade to  5.3.1 and read the  to get started.workflowidempotency documentationRead moreSubscribe to messages inside the runIdempotency with no extra code
